title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is axiomatizing a combinatorial 'analysis situs'. He works with structures M (he calls them something like 'm-géries'; the word is hard to read) whose elements are 'figures'. They carry several relations: ≤ (a figure lies in another), ≪ (lies in the closure or boundary, presumably strict), ≪° (lies in the 'interior' of, or is incident in the interior sense) and |o| (disjoint interiors). Homomorphisms f: M → M' preserve these relations.

First part, continuing the previous page. The previous page asked a lifting question. Suppose f(X) ≪° Y' ≤ f(Y) in M'. Is Y' necessarily of the form f(Y1) with X ≪° Y1 ≤ Y? Here Grothendieck isolates a sufficient condition, (**): f(X) ≪ f(Y) ⇒ X ≪ Y, i.e. f reflects ≪. He notes that (**) is not automatic but holds if f is injective. Assuming it, the argument runs as follows.
- From f(X) ≪ f(Y) we get X ≪ Y.
- The axioms of M then give some Y1 with X ≪° Y1 ≤ Y.
- Applying f gives f(X) ≪° f(Y1) ≤ f(Y). By the uniqueness implicit on the previous page, Y' = f(Y1). This settles the lifting question.
- Next, if f(X) ≪° f(Y), the same construction gives Y1 ≤ Y with f(Y1) = f(Y). Then Y1 = Y, so X ≪° Y.
- Hence (**) implies that ≪° on M is induced (reflected) from ≪ along f.
He then asks whether ≤ and |o| are reflected too. He concludes that it seems one must impose this as an additional axiom ('en sus').

Second part. He begins to classify homomorphisms f: M → Fig(P), where P is a bare set and Fig(P) is the structure of 'set-theoretic figures' on P (families of subsets).
- Such an f yields a map X ↦ |X| := |f(X)| from M to the power set 𝔓(P), the 'support' of the figure.
- Conversely, f is recovered from this map by (*): f(X) = { |Y| : Y ∈ X̃ }, where X̃ is the normalized figure of X, i.e. the set of Y ≤ X.
- So homomorphisms into Fig(P) are the same as suitable 'realization' maps M → 𝔓(P).
The next page lists the conditions making X ↦ |X| come from such a homomorphism:
- monotonicity;
- disjoint interiors for |o|-related figures;
- nonempty open cells |X|° = |X| \ |∂X|;
- |X| = ⋃_{Y≤X} |Y|°.
These are exactly the axioms for realizing a face poset as a set-theoretic cell decomposition (regular-cell-complex or stratification combinatorics, without topology). The page thus serves to define a set-theoretic 'geometric realization' of these abstract incidence structures.
errors: The step 'f(Y1) = f(Y) donc Y1 = Y' uses injectivity of f, not merely (**). If ≪ is strict, (**) cannot yield Y1 = Y from f(Y1) = f(Y). The conclusion that (**) alone implies ≪° is induced is therefore only justified for injective f, or needs an extra axiom.
The deduction f(Y1) = f(Y) from f(X) ≪° f(Y) and f(X) ≪° f(Y1) ≤ f(Y) relies on an unstated uniqueness or maximality property of ≪° (presumably from pp. 27–29). It is not justified on this page.

ideas.what: Condition that a morphism of incidence structures reflect the strict incidence relation ≪, used to lift intermediate figures and to show ≪° is reflected
ideas.modern_name: Reflection of relations / embedding-like (full) morphisms of posets or incidence structures; cellular embeddings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard order-theoretic notion; no specific credit

ideas.what: Homomorphisms M → Fig(P) are equivalent to support maps X ↦ |X| ⊂ P, with f(X) = {|Y| : Y ≤ X}; conditions (on the next page) are monotonicity, disjoint open cells, nonempty open cells, and |X| = union of open cells of faces
ideas.modern_name: Set-theoretic realization of a face poset as a (regular) cell decomposition / stratification; abstract cell complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Regular CW complexes and face posets (Björner 1984; Lundell–Weingram); abstract cell complexes (Tucker, Steinitz, Kovalevsky)
ideas.where_published: Theme of 'tame topology' and dévissage in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 Analysis situs drafts set up an axiomatic combinatorial theory of 'figures' with relations ≤, ≪, ≪°, |o'. They also treat its morphisms and its set-theoretic realizations (homomorphisms into Fig(P)). Whether ≤ and |o| are reflected under such morphisms is left open: he says it must be imposed as an additional axiom. This combinatorial-cellular foundation for tame topology was never published or developed.
missed.quote: Qu'en est-il de ≤, |o|? Il semble qu'il faille les poser en sus....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relevant to combinatorial and tame (o-minimal) foundations of stratified spaces and to face-poset realization theory. It is mainly of historical interest, as the content largely parallels known regular-cell-complex combinatorics.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine technical steps in an unpublished axiomatics of cell-like incidence structures. The realization criterion (on the next page) essentially matches known face-poset or regular-cell-complex conditions. The page is of historical interest as part of the unpublished Analysis situs, but contains no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: '= si f injectif' reads more like 'c'est le cas si f injectif' / 'OK si f injectif'; 'Si c'est vrai, et [?]' is probably 'Si c'est vrai, et si'.
'Il semble qu'il faille en poser un sens [?]....' should read 'Il semble qu'il faille les poser en sus....' (i.e. impose as extra axioms).
The target written 'Figés (P)' is uncertain. It is probably an abbreviation like 'Figens (P)' / 'Figures (P)' (set-theoretic figures on P); the next page writes 'Fig il(P)'.
In (*) the struck-out symbol before |Y| is a deleted letter; the formula is f(X) = { |Y| : Y ∈ X̃ }.
The left-margin note seems to define X̃ (something like 'où X̃ = ensemble des Y ≤ X ⊂ ...'). It is hard to read; the transcription's '𝔉(X)' is doubtful.
